useWhen: Use FEAT when the source is something a creature has, not something it carries: a feat, a class or subclass feature, a species trait, a background feature, a monster trait or action, a boon, blessing or charm, a fighting style, an eldritch invocation, a metamagic option or a maneuver.
smallest: `ITEM.Name` (the name). Nothing else is required, but write `ITEM.Feature Type` so the sheet shows the right kind of feature.
notFor: A whole class, subclass, species or background. These templates do not cover them; FEAT holds one feature at a time.
A spell, even one granted by a feat or a species: SPELL.
A monster's weapon attack (Bite, Claw, Longsword): WEAPON (`Weapon Type: natural` for a bite or claw).
A magic item: EQUIPMENT, WEAPON, CONSUMABLE, TOOL or CONTAINER.

checks: A feature has no rarity, price, weight, quantity, attunement or unidentified text. `ITEM.Rarities`, `INVENTORY`, `COST_AND_WEIGHT`, `UNIDENTIFIED_DESCRIPTION` and `ATTUNEMENT` are ignored with a warning.

`ITEM.Feature Type` is a dnd5e id: `background`, `class`, `monster`, `race`, `enchantment`, `feat`, `pietyTrait`, `supernaturalGift` or `vehicle`. A species or lineage trait is `race`. `species`, `racial` or `Class Feature` is stored as an unknown type with a warning.

`ITEM.Feature Subtype` takes only the listed subtype ids, such as `fightingStyle`, `eldritchInvocation`, `metamagic`, `maneuver`, `channelDivinity`, `general`, `origin` and `epicBoon`. Do not put the class name there. Class and level go in `ITEM.Requirements`, for example `Fighter 2`.

"Level 4+" is two fields: the text in `ITEM.Requirements` and the number in `PREREQUISITES.Level`. `PREREQUISITES.Level: 4+` fails. `PREREQUISITES.Items` takes dnd5e identifiers such as `"feat:alert"`, not display names.

A passive feature has no `USAGE` or `RECOVERY`. For limited uses, `USAGE.Uses Max` is a whole number or a quoted formula without dice, such as `"@prof"` or `"max(1, @abilities.wis.mod)"`, and `USAGE.Uses Spent` is `0` for a fresh feature.
"Short or long rest" is one `RECOVERY` entry with `Period: sr`. "3/Day" is `Period: day`. "Recharge 5-6" is `Period: recharge` with `Formula: "5"`; `"5-6"` is dropped with a warning.

`ADVANCEMENT` is one list for the whole feature. Each entry has exactly one root key: `ABILITY_SCORE_IMPROVEMENT`, `GRANT_ITEMS`, `CHOOSE_ITEMS`, `MODIFY_ITEMS`, `SCALE_VALUE` or `TRAIT`. A mapping in place of the list fails.

Trait keys use dnd5e ids: `skills:ath`, not `skills:athletics` (the importer does not catch that one); `weapon:mar`; `armor:hvy`. A granted Item is a reference to an Item that already exists in the world or a compendium: give `Name` and `Type`, and do not make up a `UUID`. The import waits until every reference is resolved.
